sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS OVER PARTS OF SRN AND ERN TX
sections.text: ...SYNOPSIS... BROAD CYCLONIC FLOW WILL CONTINUE TO PREVAIL OVER THE NRN HALF OF THE NATION...WITH MAIN TROUGH AXIS OVER THE PLNS. TO THE SOUTH...SRN STREAM UPR LOW NOW OVER BAJA CA EXPECTED TO TRACK GENERALLY ENE THROUGH THE PERIOD...REACHING NW MEXICO LATER TODAY...AND THE REGION S OF THE TX BIG BEND BY 12Z TUE. AT LWR LVLS...SFC WAVE NOW ENTERING MO...ASSOCIATED WITH UPR IMPULSE NOW IN NEB...SHOULD TRACK RAPIDLY ENEWD TODAY ALONG STALLED FRONT EXTENDING THROUGH THE OH VLY/LWR GRT LKS. THE WAVE SHOULD WEAKEN AS THE UPR DISTURBANCE DEAMPLIFIES IN THE FAST/CONFLUENT WSW FLOW.

sections.title: MID MS/OH VLYS TODAY/TNGT
sections.text: STRONG MID LVL WSW FLOW...WITH SPEEDS AOA 80 KTS AT 500 MB AND AROUND 70 KTS AT 700...WILL PREVAIL OVER THE OH VLY TODAY AND EARLY TNGT...DOWNSTREAM FROM DEAMPLIFYING UPR IMPULSE. AS THE ASSOCIATED SFC WAVE MOVES RAPIDLY ENE FROM MO...BOTH THE TRAILING COLD FRONT AND THE WARM / STNRY BOUNDARY TO ITS EAST LIKELY WILL SERVE TO FOCUS DIURNALLY ENHANCED TSTM DEVELOPMENT. SHOWERS/STORMS NOW OVER FAR ERN IL/IND APPEAR TO BE TIED TO LOW LVL WAA/MOISTURE TRANSPORT MAX ON POLEWARD SIDE OF 50 KT SWLY LLJ. THE STORMS SHOULD DIMINISH LATER THIS MORNING AS THEY MOVE/DEVELOP NEWD AWAY FROM AREA OF GREATEST INSTABILITY. DAYTIME HEATING AND CONTINUED ENE MOTION OF NEB IMPULSE WILL...NEVERTHELESS...LIKELY FOSTER A NEW ROUND OF MORE NEARLY SFC-BASED STORMS BY EARLY AFTN ALONG COLD FRONT FROM NRN/WRN IND SWWD INTO ERN/SRN IL AND SE MO. MOISTURE WILL REMAIN MODEST /SFC DEWPOINTS IN THE UPR 50S TO LWR 60S F WITH PW TO 1.25 INCHES/...MID LVL LAPSE RATES WILL NOT BE VERY STEEP...AND CLOUDS WILL TEMPER HEATING. BUT SUFFICIENT INSTABILITY /SBCAPE OF 500 TO NEAR 1000 J PER KG/ SHOULD EXIST FOR SUSTAINED STORMS. WIND PROFILES...MEANWHILE...WILL BE VERY FAVORABLE FOR SUSTAINED SUPERCELLS. THE GREATEST LIKELIH

sections.title: RIO GRAND VLY/TX HILL COUNTRY TNGT/EARLY TUE
sections.text: LOW LVL SLY FLOW/MOISTURE INFLOW WILL PERSIST OVER S TX THROUGH EARLY TUE...AHEAD OF EWD-MOVING BAJA UPR LOW. RESULTING MOIST AXIS OVER S TX SHOULD BE CHARACTERIZED BY SFC DEWPOINTS IN THE MID TO UPR 60S F AND PW UP TO 1.50 INCHES. RELATIVELY WARM MID LVL TEMPS / SHORTWAVE RIDGE AHEAD OF BAJA SYSTEM SHOULD KEEP REGION CAPPED TO TSTM DEVELOPMENT THROUGH THE DAY. TSTMS MAY...HOWEVER...MOVE/DEVELOP ACROSS THE REGION LATER TNGT OR...MORE LIKELY...EARLY TUE AS ASCENT INCREASES WITH THE APPROACH OF THE BAJA LOW. THE STORMS SHOULD FORM ON THE W EDGE OF THE MOIST AXIS FROM THE HILL COUNTRY SSW TO NEAR KDRT. WITH MLCAPE AROUND 1500 J/KG AND 50+ KT DEEP SHEAR...ENVIRONMENT COULD YIELD SUPERCELLS WITH SVR WIND...HAIL...AND PERHAPS A TORNADO. GIVEN PROGRESSIVE NATURE / STRENGTH OF FORCING FOR ASCENT...AND AMPLE MOISTURE AVAILABILITY...THE STORMS SHOULD MERGE INTO A FAIRLY EXTENSIVE LINE/QLCS. WIND DAMAGE WILL BE THE MAIN SVR THREAT THROUGH THE END OF THE PERIOD...WITH THE THREAT PERHAPS SOMEWHAT MITIGATED BY THE TIME OF DAY. ..CORFIDI/ROGERS.. 11/14/2011

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A BROADLY CYCLONIC...SPLIT FLOW REGIME WILL BE MAINTAINED OVER THE CONUS THIS PERIOD WITH A BELT OF HIGH-MOMENTUM MIDLEVEL FLOW EXTENDING FROM THE PACIFIC NW THROUGH THE NRN PLAINS INTO THE GREAT LAKES...OH VALLEY AND INTO NERN STATES. WITHIN THIS LARGER-SCALE PATTERN...SHORTWAVE TROUGH OVER THE MID MO VALLEY WILL DEAMPLIFY WHILE BECOMING ENTRAINED INTO A CONFLUENT FLOW PATTERN OVER THE GREAT LAKES AND OH VALLEY. FARTHER S...MIDLEVEL LOW --EMBEDDED WITHIN SUBTROPICAL AIRSTREAM-- WILL TRANSLATE FROM WRN MEXICO EWD INTO THE LOWER RIO GRANDE VALLEY BY TUE MORNING. IN THE LOW LEVELS...SURFACE LOW CURRENTLY OVER NERN MO WILL GRADUALLY WEAKEN WHILE DEVELOPING ENEWD ALONG WARM FRONT LIFTING NWD THROUGH THE OH VALLEY. IN ITS WAKE...A COLD FRONT WILL ADVANCE SEWD THROUGH THE OZARKS. THE SWRN EXTENSION OF THIS COLD FRONT WILL DECELERATE OVER THE SRN PLAINS LATER TODAY INTO TONIGHT IN RESPONSE TO CYCLOGENESIS OVER THE RED RIVER VALLEY.

sections.title: OH VALLEY REGION
sections.text: A BAND OF ELEVATED TSTMS IS IN PROGRESS THIS MORNING FROM CNTRL IL...THROUGH NRN IND INTO NWRN OH. WAA/MOISTURE ADVECTION IN EXIT REGION OF LLJ N OF WARM FRONT APPEAR TO BE SUSTAINING THIS ACTIVITY WHICH WILL BE CAPABLE OF SOME HAIL AND PERHAPS LOCALLY DAMAGING WIND GUSTS. BY THIS AFTERNOON...CONTINUED WARMING/MOISTENING ACROSS THE WARM SECTOR WILL SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF SURFACE-BASED STORMS...INITIALLY FROM CNTRL/SRN IL INTO CNTRL IND. AMBIENT ENVIRONMENT WILL BE CHARACTERIZED BY MLCAPE VALUES OF 500-1000 J/KG...EFFECTIVE SRH OF 150-300 M2/S2 AND EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR OF 50-70 KT...SUGGESTIVE OF SUPERCELLS AND BOWING STRUCTURES CAPABLE OF TORNADOES /SOME POSSIBLY STRONG/...DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL. GIVEN THE STRONG WIND FIELD IN PLACE...EXPECT THIS ACTIVITY TO PROGRESS RAPIDLY EWD ACROSS THE OH VALLEY THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT WITH A CONTINUED RISK FOR SEVERE WEATHER.

sections.title: LOWER RIO GRANDE VALLEY INTO TX HILL COUNTRY
sections.text: WIDESPREAD LOW CLOUDS AND THE ABSENCE OF ANY APPRECIABLE LARGE-SCALE FORCING FOR ASCENT WILL LIMIT THE POTENTIAL FOR TSTMS AND A SEVERE WEATHER THREAT THROUGH TODAY. BY TONIGHT...MIDLEVEL HEIGHTS WILL BEGIN TO FALL AHEAD OF MIDLEVEL LOW TRANSLATING ACROSS NRN MEXICO...SUPPORTING A GRADUAL INCREASE IN TSTM ACTIVITY. FORECAST SOUNDINGS SUGGEST THAT A MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER WILL COINCIDE WITH STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES...CONTRIBUTING TO MUCAPE VALUES OF 1000-1500 J/KG. GIVEN THE PRESENCE OF VERTICALLY VEERING WIND PROFILES AND 40-50 KT OF DEEP-LAYER SHEAR...SETUP WILL PROMOTE THE DEVELOPMENT OF ORGANIZED STORM STRUCTURES --INCLUDING SUPERCELLS AND BOWING LINE SEGMENTS-- WITH THE PRIMARY HAZARDS BEING SOME HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS.

sections.title: CNTRL AR INTO ERN OK AND NERN TX
sections.text: NEGLIGIBLE FORCING FOR ASCENT AND A WELL-DEFINED CAP AT THE BASE OF AN EML --PER 12Z REGIONAL SOUNDINGS-- WILL LIKELY PRECLUDE TSTM POTENTIAL THIS AFTERNOON. BY THIS EVENING INTO TONIGHT...THE COMBINATION OF CONVERGENCE ALONG THE COLD FRONT AND STRENGTHENING LOW-LEVEL WAA DOWNSTREAM FROM DEVELOPING RED RIVER FRONTAL WAVE WILL FOSTER AN INCREASE IN TSTMS. CURRENTLY...THERE IS SOME QUESTION WHETHER STORMS WILL BE ROOTED IN THE BOUNDARY LAYER OR SLIGHTLY ELEVATED ABOVE FRONTAL ZONE. IN EITHER EVENT...A LOW PROBABILITY THREAT FOR HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS WILL EXIST. HOWEVER...IF STORMS CAN BECOME SURFACE-BASED...A COMPARATIVELY GREATER RISK FOR DAMAGING WINDS...HAIL AND PERHAPS A TORNADO WILL EXIST WITH THE STRONGEST ACTIVITY. SHOULD SUBSEQUENT MODEL AND OBSERVATIONAL DATA INDICATE A HIGHER PROBABILITY OF THIS LATTER SCENARIO...A CATEGORICAL UPGRADE TO SLIGHT RISK MAY BE NECESSARY AT 20Z. ..MEAD.. 11/14/2011

sections.title: 20Z OUTLOOK UPDATE
sections.text: ...OHIO VALLEY... GIVEN THE LACK OF STRONGER MID-LEVEL FORCING FOR UPWARD VERTICAL MOTION...IT IS POSSIBLE THAT THE SEVERE PROBABILITIES...AS CURRENTLY DEPICTED IN THE WARM SECTOR OF THE WEAKENING SURFACE WAVE MIGRATING THROUGH THE OHIO VALLEY...MAY BE A BIT HIGH. HOWEVER...THE HIGH RESOLUTION RAPID REFRESH CONTINUES TO SUGGEST A WINDOW OF OPPORTUNITY FOR SCATTERED VIGOROUS BOUNDARY LAYER BASED STORM DEVELOPMENT FROM PARTS OF SOUTHEAST MISSOURI AND SOUTHERN ILLINOIS INTO OHIO BETWEEN NOW AND 01-02Z. THE LATEST RUC GUIDANCE DOES INDICATE THAT INHIBITION IS BECOMING INCREASINGLY NEGLIGIBLE FOR MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER PARCELS CHARACTERIZED BY CAPE ON THE ORDER OF 500 J/KG ACROSS THIS REGION. AND...WIND PROFILES STILL CHARACTERIZED BY STRONG DEEP LAYER MEAN FLOW AND LARGE CLOCKWISE CURVED LOW-LEVEL HODOGRAPHS WILL BE SUPPORTIVE OF ENHANCED TORNADIC/WIND DAMAGE POTENTIAL WITH ANY DEVELOPING STORMS. PRIOR OUTLOOK IS GENERALLY BEING MAINTAINED AS IS DUE TO UNCERTAINTY...BUT GREATEST SEVERE POTENTIAL MAY BE CONFINED TO THE IMMEDIATE VICINITY OF THE SURFACE WARM FRONT ACROSS NORTH CENTRAL INDIANA AND OHIO.

sections.title: CENTRAL ARKANSAS INTO ERN OK AND NERN TX
sections.text: STORM DEVELOPMENT STILL APPEARS UNLIKELY UNTIL LATE THIS EVENING AND OVERNIGHT...WHEN ACTIVITY IS EXPECTED TO BE MOSTLY ROOTED WITHIN A WARM ADVECTION REGIME...GENERALLY ABOVE A STABLE OR STABILIZING BOUNDARY LAYER. WITH LOW-LEVEL FLOW FIELDS AND SHEAR BECOMING MORE MODEST IN STRENGTH...AND NOT EXPECTED TO INCREASE APPRECIABLY TONIGHT...SUB-SLIGHT RISK SEVERE PROBABILITIES ARE BEING MAINTAINED. ..KERR.. 11/14/2011 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1023 AM CST MON NOV 14 2011/
